thread:
sarah: Heads-up — we have an urgent customer escalation from Acme (dedicated pool) reporting p95/p99 latency regressions after we flipped the int8 quantization profile on their model. They saw p95 go from ~120ms to ~420ms and p99 from ~240ms to ~1.2s during a steady traffic window. Ticket #ACME-412.

sarah: Repro steps from support (copied):
1) Send standard chat payload (seq len ~256 tokens typical).
2) Use model `redwood-rl-7b` with quant_profile `int8_aggressive` (this was just rolled to the pool last night).
3) Observe tail latency spikes and occasional timeouts.

sarah: Support attached a sample request and a few request IDs: rreq_20260301_aa31, rreq_20260301_bb12. They say spikes started ~01:10 UTC when we rolled the new profile.

jake: I'm looking at runtime traces for that pool. I see repeated kernel fallback logs around the same timestamps: `kernel_fallback: calibration_miss -> fp16_fallback` and a bunch of `kvcache_miss_ratio` bumps. That pattern often causes long tail because fallback triggers a slower execution path.

maria: Do we have the quant calibration table for that model/version? My suspicion is the `int8_aggressive` profile didn't include calibration buckets for the 256+ sequence range the customer commonly uses. When runtime sees out-of-calibration activations we do fallback to fp16 which costs us time (and sometimes forces kernel rebinds).

ashwin: I pulled the model metadata: `redwood-rl-7b@v3` was built with per-channel symmetric quant and calibration was run on sequences up to 128 tokens by default. The v3 artifact has a `quant_map` that lists bucket boundaries 1..128 only. That definitely matches the symptom.

beth: Attaching a snippet from the deploy logs near the roll time:
```
[2026-03-01T01:09:51Z] deploy: profile int8_aggressive applied to pool dedicated-acme-01
[2026-03-01T01:10:05Z] runtime: warmup completed, kernel set = int8_kernels_v2
[2026-03-01T01:10:12Z] runtime: kernel_fallback: calibration_miss -> fp16_fallback (req=rreq_20260301_aa31)
[2026-03-01T01:10:13Z] runtime: rebind kernels -> fp16_kernels_v1
[2026-03-01T01:10:15Z] monitoring: p99 latency 1200ms (window=60s)
```

beth: Also see higher GC pauses in the same window due to larger temporary buffers allocated during fallback.

jake: For quick triage I recommend we: (A) remove `int8_aggressive` from the dedicated-acme-01 pool (rollback to `fp16_safe`), (B) add a canary config that enforces `quant_calib_buckets` to include seq len up to 512 for aggressive profiles, and (C) enable a proactive pfallback metric alert so we failover earlier.

maria: Agreed. Immediate mitigation = pin Acme's routing to `redwood-rl-7b@v3+fp16_safe`. That will stop the fallback thrash. I'll prepare the rollback.

sarah: Support asked for a reproducible curl snippet; sharing the exact sample payload we used to reproduce the spike: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-rl-7b","quant_profile":"int8_aggressive","input":"<long prompt repeated to reach ~256 tokens>","max_tokens":128}'
```

ashwin: To reproduce locally in the runtime test cluster use: 
```
rictl request send --pool dedicated-acme-01 --model redwood-rl-7b --quant-profile int8_aggressive --prompt-file tests/payloads/long_prompt.txt --concurrency 10 --duration 60s
```
This will show the tail behavior quickly because concurrent requests increase chances of hitting fallback race windows.

maria: I've queued the rollback. Patch in progress: change pool config `quant_profile: fp16_safe`; add a guard where `int8_aggressive` requires `calibration_buckets_max_seq >= 512` else the profile fails validation. PR: https://git.internal/r/quant-profiles/pull/412

beth: Ops note: when we rollback, we should also clear the kernel cache on the nodes to avoid stale kernel sets. Command: 
```
runcmd --nodes pool:dedicated-acme-01 --cmd 'runtimectl kernels clear && runtimectl warmup --model redwood-rl-7b --profile fp16_safe'
```

jake: I've added an SLO alert tweak: fire when `pfallback_rate > 0.5%` for 5m in dedicated pools. That will route to oncall earlier.

support-bot: Ticket ACME-412 updated: rollback initiated by maria at 2026-03-01T01:18Z. Customer notified.

sarah: After rollback we should collect these artifacts for a postmortem:
- full runtime trace for 01:08-01:22 UTC
- the quant calibration tables for v3 artifacts
- request samples that triggered fallback (we already have two request ids)
- kernel binding logs and memory footprint graphs

ashwin: Long-term fix options: ship a stricter validation step when promoting quant profiles to pools (check calib coverage and sample sequence distribution), allow dynamic extension of calibration online (expensive), or prefer `int8_safe` which has broader buckets and slower tail but stable.

maria: For the near-term I will: 
- finish rollback (in progress)
- add validation gate to deploy pipeline (PR linked above)
- coordinate with Acme CS for a test window to re-evaluate an adjusted int8 profile
Assigning to me (maria) and cc'ing product for policy decision.

beth: After rollback completed: 
[2026-03-01T01:20:12Z] runtime: kernels cleared on 4 nodes
[2026-03-01T01:20:30Z] runtime: warmup fp16_safe completed
[2026-03-01T01:22:05Z] monitoring: p95 back to 130ms, p99 back to 260ms (window=5m)

sarah: Customer confirmed reduced tail in their next 15m window. They want a follow-up for a safe int8 trial with longer calibration.

jake: Putting an action item for infra to add a `quant_profile_dry_run` feature which runs the profile in a spectator mode (no traffic impact) and simulates fallback rate by replaying sampled requests. That would have caught this.

ashwin: Noted — I'll draft a spec. Also recommend we publish a short KB for support that describes how quantization calibration coverage affects tail latency and what to ask customers (typical seq lengths, burstiness, timeouts).

sarah: Great work team. For now ticket ACME-412 -> status: mitigated, postmortem pending. Assigning follow-ups: rollback/validation = maria, spec for dry-run = ashwin, KB + customer comms = beth.

support-bot: ACME-412 status changed to MITIGATED by maria at 2026-03-01T01:23Z.

maria: I'll update this thread with the postmortem link when ready. For the immediate doc we should include the exact metrics before/after and the calibration table diff.

sarah: Thanks everyone. If anyone spots other pools with `int8_aggressive` deployed, please flag here so we can audit calibration coverage.
